findings.message: SEC-0.5.1-01 (RESOLVED at head) — deletion-lane symlink guard re-homed in presence.gc
findings.detail_md:
**Status at head 14388175215c322f1003362462402d53be1b2e32: RESOLVED — retained as the audit trail of the finding and its verification.**

**Description.** Commit af27c9f8 (T-051-07, 'presence owns liveness and GC end-to-end; post-gate reaper deleted') removed hooks/sdd_post_gate.py's guarded reaper together with its guard implementation (_resolved_within(path, dadaia_root), os.walk(..., followlinks=False)) and its two contract tests (tests/unit/hooks/test_post_gate_reap.py::test_lane_guard_never_follows_a_symlinked_directory and ::test_lane_guard_refuses_a_target_resolving_outside_dadaia). The surviving owner, dadaia_workspace/features/spec_context/presence.py:_reap_presence_records (line 409: `sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir())`, line 434: `entry.unlink(missing_ok=True)`), treats a symlink-to-directory as a presence context dir, descends into it and unlinks the *.json entries it finds; features/spec_context/presence.py:_reap_markers (line 447-465) likewise unlinks by name prefix under .dadaia/tmp/ without resolving. The new test file tests/unit/features/spec_context/test_presence_gc.py has no symlink or boundary-escape coverage (it does retain the traversal-shaped marker-name test). Reproduced deterministically in a scratch tmp tree: with `<ws>/.dadaia/states/presence/linked-ctx -> <ws>/../OUTSIDE-dadaia` and a stale-shaped record inside it, `presence.gc(ws, now=..., own_session_id='me')` returned presence=('linked-ctx/victim',) and the file outside .dadaia/ no longer existed. Trust domain: local only — planting the symlink requires write access under .dadaia/states/presence/ (a MUTATING path any concurrent session can write), so the realistic shape is a confused-deputy amplification where one session's PostToolUse throttle cadence or `dadaia doctor --fix` deletes *.json files outside .dadaia/ on another actor's behalf. No credential, PII or authentication boundary is involved. Pre-existing at develop in the sibling lane (presence.stale_records/sweep iterate `p.is_dir()` identically), so the range widens the unguarded lane's cadence and removes the only guarded implementation rather than introducing a new class.

**Evidence.** presence.py:400-445 (reap lanes); presence.py:447-465 (marker lane); git show origin/develop:tests/unit/hooks/test_post_gate_reap.py:314-380 (the deleted AG.1 contract tests); git diff origin/develop..4ff8dcb2 -- dadaia_workspace/hooks/sdd_post_gate.py (deleted lines 176, 211-225, 268, 326, 344, 375, 405, 438); reproduction script kept out-of-repo under the session scratchpad

**Fix verified.** presence.py:124-134 (`_within_dadaia`), :420-451 (`is_symlink()` skip + per-entry containment re-check), :468-485 (marker lane re-check); regression test tests/unit/features/spec_context/test_presence_gc.py::test_symlinked_context_dir_to_outside_dadaia_never_followed. Original reproduction re-run unchanged against head: the file outside .dadaia/ survives and the presence lane reports nothing, where it previously deleted it. Note for the fixing agent: the same class still exists at develop in presence.stale_records/sweep (`p.is_dir()` without the symlink clause) and is now closed on this branch only — confirm it stays closed after the rc-1 merge.
findings.fix_recommendation: None outstanding on this head. Post-merge, re-confirm the guard is the only path both reap lanes take.

findings.message: SEC-0.5.1-02 — Verdict candidate discovery does not refuse a symlinked verdicts/ directory

**Description.** features/chokepoints/verdict.py:discover_verdict_candidates globs the two committed evidence roots and validates the release-id segment against RELEASE_SEMVER_RE (correctly refusing specs/releases/_ideas/**), but a committed symlink at specs/releases/<id>/verdicts pointing outside the repo would still be traversed by pathlib glob. **Evidence.** dadaia_workspace/features/chokepoints/verdict.py:60-92
findings.fix_recommendation: Optional: assert `not path.is_symlink()` and containment under repo_root for each candidate before accepting it.

findings.message: SEC-0.5.1-03 — Privacy-pattern threading defaults to an empty sequence on the BugRecord transitions
findings.detail_md:
**Description.** core/models/bugs.py's resolve/supersede/defer/reject take `privacy_patterns: Sequence[PatternLike] = ()`, so a caller that forgets to thread the operator baseline performs no privacy check at all (fail-open default). The only production caller is correct today: cli/commands/bugs.py:107 passes container.load_denylist_baseline_patterns() into BugService, and features/bugs/service.py:212 threads self._baseline_patterns through the single `transition` seam for all four methods. Refusal messages carry only the pattern's `reason`, never the offending value (CWE-532 respected).

**Evidence.** dadaia_workspace/core/models/bugs.py:333, 383, 412, 427, 440; dadaia_workspace/features/bugs/service.py:96-110, 195-215; dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/bugs.py:107
findings.fix_recommendation: Optional hardening: make privacy_patterns a required keyword so a future second caller cannot silently opt out of the check.

findings.message: SEC-0.5.1-05 — security-verdict-gate now installs the package (pip install -e .) from the PR head before running the gate
findings.detail_md:
**Description.** ci.yml's security-verdict-gate gains a setup-python + `pip install -e .` step so the gate can run `dadaia ci verdict-check` instead of a 336-line bash re-implementation. This executes PR-head packaging metadata inside the gate job. The job keeps workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`, is a `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`) trigger, holds no secrets, and every other CI job already executes PR-head code, so no new trust boundary is crossed. The replacement is a net security improvement: the sha is shape-checked as 40-hex and the release id against the canon pattern before either reaches a git argv, and the release-id segment check refuses the freely-writable specs/releases/_ideas/ tree as a verdict root.

**Evidence.** .github/workflows/ci.yml:530-552; .github/scripts/pr-verdict-check.sh (336 -> 27 lines); dadaia_workspace/cli/commands/ci.py:315-383
findings.fix_recommendation: None. Note for the operator: this gate is advisory on rc-1's own PR (the PR that introduces the job) and must be made required from rc-2 by re-supplying the whole required-status-checks list.
